questions.question: A flow network has source $s$, sink $t$ and a feasible flow. Which object is an augmenting path for this flow?
options: An $s$–$t$ path in the original network, every edge below capacity
An $s$–$t$ path in the residual network, every direction positive
Any path from $s$ in the residual network with positive residuals
An $s$–$t$ path in the residual network with positive total residual

questions.question: An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. How is its residual capacity (bottleneck) $\delta$ defined?
options: $\delta=\sum_{e} r_e$, the total residual on the path
$\delta=\max_{e} r_e$, the largest residual on the path
$\delta=r_{e_1}$, the residual of the first direction
$\delta=\min_{e} r_e$, the least residual on the path

questions.question: An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. Flow is augmented along the path by its bottleneck $\delta=\min_e r_e$. What happens to the value of the source-to-sink flow?
options: It increases by the sum of all $r_e$.
It becomes equal to $\delta$ itself.
It increases by $\delta$ per path edge.
It increases by exactly $\delta$ units.

questions.question: An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. Why is the amount sent along the path limited to $\delta=\min_e r_e$?
options: More would exceed the residual of some direction on the path.
Any amount up to the sum of the residuals would also be fine.
The minimum is only a convention; the maximum $r_e$ also works.
Smaller amounts are preferred because they keep the flow integer.

questions.question: An augmenting path traverses the reverse direction $A\to B$ of the original edge $B\to A$, which carries flow $x_{BA}=5$. The flow is augmented by $\delta=3$. What is the new flow on $B\to A$?

Along an augmenting path in a residual network, every direction $e$ has residual capacity $r_e>0$, and $\delta=\min_e r_e$ units are sent. What happens to the residual capacities of the path's directions?
options: Exactly one of them drops to 0.
At least one of them drops to 0.
Every one of them drops to 0.
None drops to 0; each keeps room.

questions.question: An augmenting path is a source-to-sink path in the residual network of a feasible flow, with residual capacity $r_e>0$ in each traversed direction $e$. It traverses one reverse direction, which lowers the flow on that original edge by its bottleneck $\delta$. What happens to the source-to-sink flow value?
options: It stays the same, as $+\delta$ and $-\delta$ cancel.
It falls by $\delta$, as some flow is cancelled.
It rises by $2\delta$, counting both kinds of step.
It rises by $\delta$, as for any augmenting path.
